rounds.text: Share India Securities Ltd trades at a compelling valuation with a P/E of 11.2x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of just 2.86x against a sector benchmark of 12.95x [E11], significantly undercutting broader sector multiples. The business delivers exceptional profitability and capital efficiency, boasting an ROE of 12.81% and ROCE of 16.53% that comfortably outpace sector benchmarks of 5.44% and 5.84% respectively [E9, E10], alongside a 10-year median ROE of 23% [E25]. This strong operational performance is backed by historical scale, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded sales growth of 35% and a 10-year compounded profit growth of 48% [E14, E18]. A discounted cash flow model suggests massive intrinsic value headroom with a 72.6% margin of safety at the current price of ₹ 188 [E2, E45], while a reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in a mere 0.1% earnings growth [E46]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -182 Cr in March 2026 alongside a cash conversion ratio of -0.56x [E33, E34], and promoters have pledged 40.4% of their holding [E61].

Share India Securities faces significant structural risks that undermine its seemingly attractive valuation metrics. The company’s financial health is compromised by a severe cash flow crisis, evidenced by negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -182 Cr and Rs -186 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E34, E35]. This is compounded by a concerning rise in borrowings to Rs 948 Cr from Rs 695 Cr in the prior year [E38] and a massive contingent liability of Rs 6,466 Cr [E60]. Furthermore, the quality of ownership is deteriorating, as promoter holdings have declined by 4.19% over the last three years [E62], with 40.4% of their remaining stake currently pledged [E61]. While the company has historically shown growth, profit expansion has stalled, with 0% compounded profit growth over the last three years [E20] and a clear deceleration in earnings [E68]. Conceded: the company maintains a low P/E ratio of 11.2x [E1] and strong historical ROCE of 18.4% [E12]. Despite these figures, the combination of negative institutional money flow [E43] and a history of extreme volatility, including a 70.2% peak-to-trough drawdown [E52], suggests that the market’s skepticism is well-founded.

The bear’s focus on cash flow [E34, E35] ignores the company’s robust liquidity, as evidenced by a current ratio of 2.35x [E37] and a strong ROCE of 18.4% [E12], which significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 5.84% [E10]. While the bear highlights rising borrowings [E38], the debt-to-equity ratio remains at a moderate 0.33x [E36], indicating that leverage is well-managed relative to the company's scale. Conceded: the company has contingent liabilities of Rs 6,466 Cr [E60] and promoter pledges of 40.4% [E61]. However, the bear’s claim of stalled profit growth is contradicted by the trailing twelve-month profit growth of 34% [E21] and a 10-year compounded profit growth of 48% [E18], proving the business remains in a long-term expansionary phase. The market’s skepticism is arguably a mispricing, as the stock trades at an EV/EBITDA of 2.86x against a sector benchmark of 12.95x [E11], suggesting the current valuation fails to reflect the company's fundamental efficiency. Finally, the negative institutional flow [E43] is countered by the company’s strong relative-strength rating of 82 against the Nifty 500 [E50], demonstrating that the stock maintains significant underlying momentum despite institutional caution.

The bull’s reliance on a current ratio of 2.35x [E37] to dismiss cash flow concerns is misplaced, as it ignores the reality that the company generated negative operating cash flow of Rs -182 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -186 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. While the bull cites a moderate debt-to-equity ratio [E36], it fails to address that borrowings have surged to Rs 948 Cr from Rs 695 Cr in just one year [E38], a trend that compounds the risk posed by the massive Rs 6,466 Cr in contingent liabilities [E60]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong ROCE of 18.4% [E12] and a 10-year profit growth rate of 48% [E18]. However, the bull’s claim of an expansionary phase is undermined by the fact that 3-year compounded profit growth has stalled at 0% [E20] and operating margins are trending inconsistently [E31, E32]. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on relative strength [E50] ignores the reality of negative institutional money flow [E43, E69] and the concerning 40.4% of promoter holdings that are currently pledged [E61]. Finally, the bull’s reliance on valuation multiples [E11] fails to account for the -70.2% historical drawdown risk [E52], which suggests that the market’s skepticism may be a rational response to the company's volatile cash position and declining promoter commitment [E40, E62].
